translations.idiomatic: Zhangling said: "Would real conspirators announce their names and the date of their plot?

sentences.zh: 此移禍也。」

translations.literal: This is shifting blame onto others.'
translations.idiomatic: This is an attempt to shift blame onto others."

sentences.zh: 诇知果出邀功者，欲藉興大獄，遂置不問。

translations.literal: Investigation showed it truly came from someone seeking merit; he wished to use it to launch a major case, so Zhangling left the matter alone.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation showed the placards came from someone seeking credit; hoping to launch a major prosecution, he had posted them. Zhangling left the matter alone.

sentences.zh: 調江寧布政使，乞歸養親。

translations.literal: Transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangning, he requested leave to return home and care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangning, he asked to retire and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 十五年，母喪服闋，補福建布攻使，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when mourning for his mother ended, he was appointed financial commissioner of Fujian and transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1835), when his mourning for his mother ended, he was appointed financial commissioner of Fujian and transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1836) he was appointed governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 黔民苦訟累而多盜，以聽斷緝捕課吏，設旬報為考覈。

translations.literal: The people of Qian suffered from litigation burdens and there were many bandits; he made hearing cases and pursuit of bandits the standard for evaluating clerks, and established ten-day reports for assessment.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guizhou were burdened by litigation and banditry was rampant; he made case adjudication and bandit pursuit the standard for evaluating officials and required ten-day progress reports.

sentences.zh: 十八年，仁懷奸民穆繼賢糾四川綦江匪肆劫，遣兵與川軍會剿，焚其巢，首從並就殲擒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the scoundrel Mu Jixian of Renhuai gathered bandits from Qijiang, Sichuan, for widespread robbery; Zhangling sent troops to join Sichuan forces in joint suppression, burned their lair, and leaders and followers were all destroyed and captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1838) the ruffian Mu Jixian of Renhuai rallied bandits from Qijiang in Sichuan for widespread robbery; Zhangling sent troops to join Sichuan forces, burned their hideout, and killed or captured leaders and followers alike.

sentences.zh: 郎岱、普安、清鎮諸縣多種罌粟，拔除申禁，勸民種木棉，玉屏、婺川皆有成效。

translations.literal: Langdai, Pu'an, Qingzhen, and other counties widely cultivated opium poppy; he uprooted it and proclaimed the ban, urged the people to plant cotton, and at Yuping and Wuchuan there were results.
translations.idiomatic: Langdai, Pu'an, Qingzhen, and other counties widely grew opium poppy; he uprooted the crops, enforced the ban, urged the people to plant cotton, and achieved results at Yuping and Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 黔省安置流犯三千餘人，與苗民錯處，釁隙易生，疏請改發新疆；

translations.literal: More than three thousand exiles were settled in Guizhou province, living intermixed with Miao people so that friction easily arose; he memorialized to transfer them to Xinjiang;
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand exiles were settled in Guizhou, living intermixed with Miao people and breeding friction; he memorialized to transfer them to Xinjiang;

sentences.zh: 又以鎮遠、黎平、都勻、古州苗俗桀驁，以盜為生，州縣差役緝捕難週，疏請綠營每百名內精選數名，分隸府、廳、州、縣文員管轄，勤加訓練，專司捕盜：並下部議行。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the Miao of Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou were fierce and made robbery their livelihood, while county runners found pursuit difficult to cover, he memorialized that from every hundred Green Standard troops several elite men be chosen, assigned under civil officials of prefectures, departments, and counties, diligently trained, and charged solely with catching bandits—all referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that because the Miao of Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou were fierce and lived by robbery while county runners could not patrol effectively, several elite soldiers should be selected from every hundred Green Standard troops, assigned to civil officials at each level, trained diligently, and charged solely with catching bandits—all referred to the ministry for approval.

sentences.zh: 長齡治黔九載，振興文教，貴陽、銅仁、安順、石阡四府，普安、八寨、郎岱、松桃四廳，黃平、普定，天柱、永從、甕安、清平、興義、普安諸州縣，皆建書院義學；

translations.literal: Zhangling governed Qian for nine years and revived culture and education; at the four prefectures of Guiyang, Tongren, Anshun, and Shiqian, the four departments of Pu'an, Bazhai, Langdai, and Songtao, and the districts and counties of Huangping, Puding, Tianzhu, Yongcong, Weng'an, Qingping, Xingyi, and Pu'an—all established academies and charity schools;
translations.idiomatic: During nine years governing Guizhou, Zhangling revived culture and education, establishing academies and charity schools in the prefectures of Guiyang, Tongren, Anshun, and Shiqian, the departments of Pu'an, Bazhai, Langdai, and Songtao, and the districts and counties of Huangping, Puding, Tianzhu, Yongcong, Weng'an, Qingping, Xingyi, and Pu'an;

sentences.zh: 省會書院分上內外三舍，親試考覈，刊刻經籍，頒行州縣。

translations.literal: the provincial academy was divided into upper, inner, and outer three halls; he personally examined and assessed students, printed classics, and distributed them to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: at the provincial capital academy he divided students into upper, inner, and outer halls, examined them personally, printed classical texts, and distributed them throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢雲貴總督，兼署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and concurrently acted as governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang (1845) he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and concurrently acted as governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 漢、回連歲互鬥，永昌回變敗退後，复圖攻城，城回謀內應，迤西道羅天池悉捕誅之。

translations.literal: Han and Hui had fought year after year; after the Yongchang Hui rebellion was defeated and retreated, they again plotted to storm the city; Hui within the city planned internal collusion, and Circuit Intendant Luo Tianchi captured and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Hui communities had fought year after year; after the Yongchang Muslim rebellion was defeated and withdrew, rebels again plotted to storm the city, and Muslims inside the walls planned to open the gates; Circuit Intendant Luo Tianchi captured and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 長齡親往督剿，擊走叛回，以肅清入告。

translations.literal: Zhangling went in person to direct suppression, drove off the rebel Hui, and reported the area pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangling went in person to direct operations, drove off the rebel Muslims, and reported the region pacified.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，回眾藉口善良不別，复叛，自請議處，撤銷獎敘，赴大理、永昌督剿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Hui masses, citing failure to distinguish the innocent from the guilty, rebelled again; he requested disciplinary action against himself, had his merit rewards revoked, and went to Dali and Yongchang to direct suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year (1846) the Muslims rebelled again, claiming the innocent had not been distinguished from the guilty; Zhangling asked to be disciplined, surrendered his merit rewards, and went to Dali and Yongchang to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 匪尋竄散，請免投誠張富罪，軍犯王芝異團練出力，亦請釋回。

translations.literal: The bandits soon scattered; he requested pardon for Zhang Fu who had surrendered, and for the military convict Wang Zhiyi who had aided the militia, also asking that he be released.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon scattered; he asked pardon for Zhang Fu, who had surrendered, and for the military convict Wang Zhiyi, who had aided the militia, requesting that he too be released.

sentences.zh: 詔斥其庸懦，降補河南布政使。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked his mediocrity and cowardice and demoted him to financial commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked his weakness and cowardice and demoted him to financial commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1847) he asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 滇回复擾雲州，多屬永昌遺孽，且得羅天池濫殺狀，追論長齡，褫職。

translations.literal: Yunnan Hui again harassed Yunzhou, mostly remnants of Yongchang; moreover the facts of Luo Tianchi's indiscriminate killing came to light, and Zhangling was pursued for review and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan Muslims again raided Yunzhou, mostly remnants of the Yongchang rebellion; when Luo Tianchi's indiscriminate killings came to light, Zhangling was investigated and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陳若霖、戴三錫盡心民事，而三錫久任蜀疆，治效較多。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Chen Ruolin and Dai Sanxi devoted themselves to the people's affairs, but Sanxi served long in the Shu frontier and his governing achievements were the greater.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Chen Ruolin and Dai Sanxi both devoted themselves to civil administration, but Sanxi's long service in Sichuan produced the greater results.

sentences.zh: 孫爾準、程祖洛先後治閩有聲，寬嚴殊途，其相濟之道乎？

translations.literal: Sun Erzhun and Cheng Zuluo in succession governed Fujian with renown; leniency and severity took different paths—is this how they complemented each other?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Erzhun and Cheng Zuluo governed Fujian in turn with distinction; one lenient, one severe—was that how they complemented each other?

sentences.zh: 裕泰兩殄楚寇，勳施爛然。

translations.literal: Yu Tai twice exterminated Chu bandits; his merit shone brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tai twice crushed rebellions in Huguang, and his achievements shone brightly.

sentences.zh: 賀長齡儒而不武，不足以奠岩疆也。

translations.literal: He Zhangling was a scholar without martial ability, insufficient to secure the rocky frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhangling was a scholar without military ability, unfit to secure a troubled frontier.
